thread.title: UPDATE: 'Get Out' and 'Dunkirk' get second runs in theaters after Oscar nominations

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: 'Get Out' and 'Dunkirk' get second runs in theaters after Oscar nominations
text:
By Trey Williams, MarketWatch
'Get Out' grossed $254.7 million at box offices worldwide on just a $4.5 million production budget
It has been almost a year since "Get Out" opened in theaters. The Jordan Peele-directed social thriller, or documentary as Peele has joked (https://twitter.com/JordanPeele/status/930796561302540288?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw&ref_url=http%3A%2F%2Fwpcomwidgets.com%2F%3Fwidth%26height%26frameborder%3D0%26style%26class%3Dtwitter-tweet%26scrolling%3Dno%26webkitallowfullscreen%26mozallowfullscreen%26allowfullscreen%26resize%3D0%26replace_attributes%3D1%26fallback%3D%253Cp%2Bclass%253D%2522protected-embed-fallback%2522%253EThis%2Bembed%2Bis%2Binvalid%253C%252Fp%253E%26_data%3DPGJsb2NrcXVvdGUgY2xhc3M9InR3aXR0ZXItdHdlZXQiIGRhdGEtbGFuZz0iZW4iPgo8cCBsYW5nPSJlbiIgZGlyPSJsdHIiPuKAmEdldCBPdXTigJkgaXMgYSBkb2N1bWVudGFyeS48L3A%252B4oCUIEpvcmRhbiBQZWVsZSAoQEpvcmRhblBlZWxlKSA8YSBocmVmPSJodHRwczovL3R3aXR0ZXIuY29tL0pvcmRhblBlZWxlL3N0YXR1cy85MzA3OTY1NjEzMDI1NDAyODg%252FcmVmX3NyYz10d3NyYyU1RXRmdyI%252BTm92ZW1iZXIgMTUsIDIwMTc8L2E%252BCjwvYmxvY2txdW90ZT4KPHNjcmlwdCBhc3luYyBzcmM9Imh0dHBzOi8vcGxhdGZvcm0udHdpdHRlci5jb20vd2lkZ2V0cy5qcyIgY2hhcnNldD0idXRmLTgiPjwvc2NyaXB0Pg%253D%253D%252Cf22f6da10e20790736c86e359e7d2544f847aa88%26_tag%3Dprotected-iframe%26_hash%3D545cb2364a7dd704909211b8b445d0dc), came out Feb. 24, 2017 -- which also happened to be Oscar weekend.
Earlier this week, the film earned four Oscar nominations from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences: Best picture, best director (Peele), best actor (Daniel Kaluuya) and best original screenplay.
"Get Out," with a budget of just $4.5 million, grossed $254.7 million at box offices worldwide for Comcast Corp.'s (CMCSA) Universal Pictures. Now, on the heels of the film's most recent success, it's getting a second run in theaters.
See:The complete list of Oscar nominations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oscars-the-complete-list-of-2018-nominees-2018-01-23)
Also read:Two theaters or 1,000? How to release an Oscar-winning film (https://www.marketwatch.com/graphics/how-to-release-an-oscar-winning-film/)
"Get Out" and "Dunkirk," which was released in July by Time Warner Inc.-owned (TWX) Warner Bros., are the only 2018 best picture-nominated films that are no longer in theaters.
A spokesman for AMC Entertainment Holdings Inc. (AMC), the largest theater chain in the U.S., said both films will be in more than 100 theaters starting Jan. 29.
The other seven best picture nominees, all currently showing in theaters, will add screens, according to AMC. Each film will be at anywhere from 200 to 500 AMC cinemas.
Check out:How Oscar nominee 'Shape of Water' was made for just $20 million (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/how-the-shape-of-water-was-made-for-just-20-million-2017-11-29)
Studios regularly increase the number of screens and theaters their films are in if they earn a best picture Oscar nomination.
Read:'Shape of Water' leads Oscar nominations with 13 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/shape-of-water-leads-oscar-nominations-with-13-2018-01-23)
"It's a way of keeping your film front and center in the minds of moviegoers and Academy voters," ComScore media analyst Paul Dergarabedian said. "If you have a film that's Oscar worthy, you kind of have to do it. It's easily the best marketing hook you can have."
It's not often, however, that films already done with their theatrical run and on home video are re-released.
According to data from ComScore, the last time a best picture nominee was released back into theaters the weekend after nominations was "Gladiator" in 2001. The film earned $72,892 that weekend and went on to win the Oscar.
Warner Bros. re-released "Mad Max: Fury Road" after it was nominated in 2015, but not until December the following year.
But expanding the number of theaters a film is in on the heels of Oscar nominations can turn a small movie into a huge success, Dergarabedian said.
Don't miss:When are the 2018 Oscars? (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/when-will-the-2018-oscar-nominations-be-announced-2018-01-19)
Last year, A24's Oscar-winning film "Moonlight" had earned $593,851 the weekend before the Academy announced the nominations. In the following weekend, A24 added more than 600 theaters and the film pulled in $1.5 million, a 151% increase. It went on to gross $64.0 million worldwide on a $4.0 million budget.

Nov. 25, 2016 $1.8 million N/A $2.3 million 33% "Manchester by the Sea" Roadside Attractions Nov. 18, 2016 $948,910 625 $2.1 million 118% ComScore
The last time "Get Out" was showing in a theater was back in June, and "Dunkirk" finished its theatrical run in November, after grossing $525.6 million worldwide. Both films are already available on home video -- "Get Out" on HBO and "Dunkirk" on Amazon (AMZN) and iTunes (AAPL).
Oscar nominations can help raise films' profiles on home video. The HBO Go platform, for example, has "Get Out" featured as an Oscar nominee on the home page. But it often doesn't generate the same level of buzz as if a movie was in theaters.
Read:Oscars academy issues code of conduct for members after Weinstein expulsion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oscars-academy-issues-code-of-conduct-for-members-after-weinstein-expulsion-2017-12-07)
Also see:MoviePass reveals its true ambitions at Sundance (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/moviepass-reveals-its-true-ambitions-at-sundance-2018-01-22)
"Do you know how powerful of a film you have to be to get attention a year after being released?" Dergarabedian said. "It's the movies that are the freshest that get attention.
"Studios spend lots of money on campaigning because they think it's worth it, so even if they ultimately lose money [putting a film back in theaters] I think this is worth it."
In addition to expanding the number of theaters for seven of the best picture nominees, and re-releasing "Get Out" and "Dunkirk," AMC will also have two best picture showcases on Feb. 24 and March 3, where they screen all nine nominees in certain theaters.
-Trey Williams;
